content.comment_body: Hello forum, I am currently building a tank cooling system and have encountered an issue. The plan is to measure the temperature of 10 tanks using PT100/PT1000 sensors. Valves for cooling water should open or close based on the temperature selected at the touch panel. However, with a [product_name] device, I can only connect a maximum of 3 [product_name] modules (which provides 6 analog inputs). My idea is to network 2 [product_name] units, allowing for a total of 5 [product_name] modules. Would this setup work? How would I access and communicate with the analog inputs on the second [product_name] device?

analysis.insight_summary: The user is designing a temperature-controlled cooling solution for 10 tanks using RTD sensors, but is limited by the analog input capacity of a single [product_name] device. To overcome this, the user considers connecting two [product_name] units in order to expand the number of analog inputs, but is unsure about how to enable communication and input addressing between the devices. The main challenge is the restricted module expandability when handling more complex installations.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects that networking two [product_name] units will allow access to all necessary analog inputs for their cooling system. They seek straightforward instructions or support on expanding I/O capacity and simple inter-device communication.
